findings.title: Docked topic title can push header controls off-screen
findings.body: .extra-info-wrapper is now a flex item of .d-header .contents (order 2) but never sets min-width: 0, flex-shrink, or overflow. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so a long topic title's min-content width cannot shrink. margin-left: auto on .panel then cannot keep the header icons in view: the row overflows and the panel is pushed past the viewport. The old float layout did not have this min-content floor. Give the wrapper flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden (and ellipsis on the title) so the title truncates and the panel stays on screen.

findings.title: Small-action description no longer fills the row
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex row, but .small-action-desc stays at the default flex: 0 1 auto and only has padding: 0 1.5%, replacing the old block padding (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em) that made the description full width beside the floated avatar. A flex item sizes to its content, so the button rule float: right (line 306) only floats inside that shrink-wrapped box, not to the right edge of the action row. Delete/expand controls that used to sit on the far right will sit immediately after the action text. Set flex: 1 1 auto and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc (or margin-left: auto on the button if it is a flex item).

findings.title: order() mixin is off-by-one for 2009 flexbox
findings.body: @mixin order writes the same $val to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as to the modern order property. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (the initial value is 1), while order is 0-based (initial value 0). Autoprefixer and the usual Discourse mixin emit $val + 1 for the ordinal-group properties. As written, order(1) is a no-op in old WebKit (same as the default group), and order(0) or a negative order cannot be represented. Header .panel uses order(3) and .extra-info-wrapper uses order(2); those still sort after untouched siblings only by accident. Fix the two box-ordinal-group lines to $val + 1 so the prefixed output matches order.
